articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka complains about the smell of marijuana during her U.S. Open match
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka, the two-time defending U.S. Open champion, complained to the chair umpire that the smell of marijuana was bothering her early in her third-round victory over Kamilla Rakhimova on Friday.
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka finally found something that could stop her at the U.S. Open: the smell of marijuana. The two-time defending champion complained to the chair umpire that it was bothering her early in her third-round victory over Kamilla Rakhimova on Friday. Sabalenka said she had never smelled the odor so strong as she did while serving early in the match. “I don’t know if it was, like, coming from the crowd or was from the outside because the wind blows it into the stadium,” Sabalenka said. “I don’t know. I just hope they’re going to be a bit more aware of that stuff.” Sabalenka was serving in the third game of the match in Louis Armstrong Stadium. She tossed the ball but then let it fall to the court. She did the same thing on the next point, with something clearly bothering her. She then approached the chair to ask for help. “I was like, guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please, to not do it around the tennis courts,” Sabalenka said, when asked what she was thinking of the time. “It’s a bit tricky to handle that smell while you’re trying to compete at your best.” Other players, such as Nick Kyrgios and Maria Sakkari, have complained in the past about the smell of marijuana during their matches. There is a park behind the grounds where the U.S. Open is played, which is often the expected source of the smell. No fans were found to be smoking and ejected from the tennis grounds. “While we can’t control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this facility as a smoke free environment,” U.S. Tennis Association spokesman Brendan McIntyre said in a statement. “This includes enforcement by our security and guest services teams when they are made aware of any individual that may be smoking, making them aware that although it may be legal in NY, that smoking is not permitted on parks property including the tennis center.” The top-seeded Sabalenka eventually was able to laugh off the topic during her news conference after the match, including the idea that fans just might be looking for ways to further enjoy her matches. “Maybe it’s too fast so they want to slow down a little bit, so who knows,” she said. “I don’t know the effect from it.”

images.caption: Belarus's Aryna Sabalenka reacts after a point against Uzbekistan's Kamilla Rakhimova during their women's singles third round tennis match on day six of the US Open tennis tournament at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in New York City on September 4, 2026.

articles.title: US Open says 2 influencers whose credentials were revoked were 'improperly submitted' as vendor staff
articles.summary: Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens, who run 'The VIP List,' claimed that their credentials were withdrawn after they posted a video of the passes, but the tournam...
articles.body:
Amid the debate around influencers at the 2026 US Open, the tournament is pushing back on two influencers who say they lost access after posting their credentials in a video.

Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens, two influencers who run New York restaurant and lifestyle account "The VIP List," claimed on Thursday that their US Open credentials had been revoked just two hours after posting the video.

However, in a statement to The Athletic on Friday, US Open head Brendan McIntyre said that Radice and Jongens were incorrectly credentialed. (McIntyre is also the managing director of the U.S. Tennis Association (USTA) and the head of USA Tennis content and communications.)

"These individuals were not credentialed as media or content creators," McIntyre told The Athletic. "They were improperly submitted for credentials on a staff list provided by a food vendor."

In a video posted on their social media on Thursday, Radice and Jongens said that they are "diehard tennis fans" and called it their "dream" to be credentialed for the event. They even acknowledged the rash of stories about influencers at the tournament, but said that it did not apply to them.

"We were there to be respectful and follow the rules and have a good time," Jongens said.

"And it was taken away, just because we wanted to show how hot we looked in our credentials," Radice added.

The influencer issue has been widespread at this year's tournament, thanks in part to an increase in credentials being offered. 54 content creators were credentialed as media in 2025, but the number nearly doubled this year to around 100, per multiple reports.

Historically, the US Open has tended to be among the rowdier Grand Slams, with the tournament encouraging crowd noise in a stark contrast to the quiet stands at Wimbledon and Roland-Garros. However, things have appear to be worse this year: Naomi Osaka's first-round match had to be paused after multiple influencers filmed and did photoshoots during play, to the point that the chair umpire had to ask them to take a seat.

Multiple players have weighed in on the issue, including Osaka, who told reporters on Thursday that she wanted people to "respect the sport" even if they were new to it.

"I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport. Especially the etiquette. I feel like it could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like in my first round match," Osaka said. "Overall, I think there's huge positives … You want people to continue to grow the sport. I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette."

Coco Gauff, who was also asked about the issue on Thursday, echoed Osaka about etiquette, though she said that she was "one of the more lenient" players about noise in the arena.

"I think it's great to have a different demographic to the sport. I have no problem with influencers. I've met some of them and follow some of them online," Gauff said. "It's not just for the players but for the viewing experience, for those around … I definitely think it's cool to have a new demographic and I definitely think it helps grow the sport. But like with anything, any venue you go to, like if you're being invited to a red carpet, you wouldn't show up in jeans.

Earlier this week, Daniil Medvedev told reporters that there is "a lot more upside than downside" to their presence.

"The more we try to raise awareness about tennis, the better it is. The more popular the sport is. For sure there is some downside," he said. "But in general the more the sport grows the better it is. I trust USTA with what they're doing."

articles.title: World No.1 Aryna Sabalenka says she might 'get high' herself if the smell of marijuana at the US Open doesn't stop drifting into the stadium
articles.summary: Tennis News: World No.1 Aryna Sabalenka humorously addresses the cannabis scent wafting through the US Open, impacting her match performance. Discover how she’s handling the situation while eyeing her next challenge.
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka has joked that she might “get high” herself if the cannabis smell keeps drifting around the US Open after briefly stopping her third-round match to complain about it.The world No.1 was playing Kamilla Rakhimova in Louis Armstrong Stadium when she noticed the strong smell and approached chair umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore while leading 3-0 in the opening set.Sabalenka ultimately brushed off the interruption and produced one of her strongest performances of the tournament, beating Rakhimova 6-3, 6-4 to reach the fourth round without dropping a set.But the cannabis smell came up again in her post-match press conference, where Sabalenka revealed just how noticeable it had been.Sabalenka explains why she stopped the matchSabalenka initially believed the smell could have been coming from somewhere in the crowd.While leading 3-0, she called over Asderaki-Moore and told the umpire: “Someone is smoking weed, do you mind … because it’s so strong.”Officials briefly searched the crowd, although they were unable to identify the source.Speaking afterwards, Sabalenka said she had no issue with people enjoying themselves away from the competition.“I was like, guys you can do whatever. You can smoke, whatever. You can relax as much as you can. But please don’t do it around the tennis courts,” she said.“It’s a bit tricky to handle that smell while you’re trying to compete at your best.”The Belarusian was then asked how “high” she was compared with the other Grand Slam tournaments, prompting a laugh and a joke that suggested the smell had already become difficult to escape.“High? The level?” Sabalenka said. “Now I can only hear weed stuff. If they’re gonna keep smoking I might get high.”Sabalenka was also asked whether it was the first time she had encountered such a strong smell while playing in New York.“That strong? Yeah,” she replied.She suggested the wind may have played a part, leaving her uncertain about exactly where the smell had come from.“Also because it was a bit windy. I don’t know if it was coming from the crowd or the outside because wind blows it into the stadium,” Sabalenka said.“I just hope they’re gonna be a bit more aware of that stuff.”Cannabis is legal in New York, and the smell has become a familiar talking point around the US Open in recent years. However, smoking is prohibited inside the tournament grounds.British player Katie Boulter had also spoken about smelling cannabis around the outer courts earlier in the tournament, saying she had experienced it while playing on Court 17.Sabalenka finds her rhythm as Townsend awaitsThe interruption did little to derail Sabalenka's progress.The two-time defending US Open champion faced a challenging test from Rakhimova but eventually came through in straight sets, backed by a superb serving display.She hit 10 aces, faced zero break points and moved into the round of 16 without dropping a set.That is significant given the form Sabalenka brought into New York. The world No.1 had not reached another final since winning Indian Wells and Miami back-to-back in March, leaving her searching for consistency as she attempted to defend her title.She is also fighting to retain the No.1 ranking. Sabalenka has held the top spot for 97 weeks, but will lose it unless she wins her third consecutive US Open title and world No.2 Elena Rybakina loses before the semi-finals.Her next opponent will be home favourite Taylor Townsend, who reached the fourth round for a second consecutive year.Townsend followed up her run to the last 16 at last year's US Open by producing another impressive tournament in New York, defeating 15th seed Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-7 (3), 6-3.That means Sabalenka now has a considerably tougher test ahead, but after arriving at the US Open short of her best form, she is beginning to find some rhythm.And if the tennis continues to improve, perhaps the only thing Sabalenka will need to worry about in her next match is the opponent — rather than what is drifting in from somewhere around the stadium.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: US Open: Serena and Venus Williams fall in first-round thriller vs. Maya Joint and Hao-ching Chan
articles.summary: The Williams sisters are a combined 4-24 in singles and doubles in 2026.
articles.body:
The Williams sisters will be a one-off show at the US Open this year. That doesn't mean it wasn't a fun time for a crowd that hadn't seen Venus and Serena team up in four years.

The 14-time Grand Slam doubles champions lost their first-round match in the women's doubles event on Friday, falling 6-3, 6-7, 7-6 in a three-hour thriller to the No. 14 seeded pair of Maya Joint and Hao-ching Chan.

With Serena not participating in the singles draw and Venus losing in the first round to Sofia Kenin , they have no more matches to play at Flushing Meadows. Serena also participated in the mixed doubles event last week, winning and losing a match alongside Carlos Alcaraz .

Joint and Chan will face Nicole Fossa Huergo and Tamara Korpatsch in the second round.

Obviously, the Williams sisters didn't display the form that won them two doubles titles at the US Open in 1999 and 2009, not with Venus at 46 years old and Serena at 44 and playing competitive tennis for only the past three months. That didn't mean they didn't have their moments. They built momentum as the match progressed and held a 5-0 lead in the decisive tiebreak, only for Joint and Chan to charge back in the face of a crowd heavily against them.

It was the kind of atmosphere we haven't seen in a Grand Slam doubles match in years. The 20-year-old Joint, who also beat Serena in the lone singles match of her comeback, appreciated the opportunity.

"[Serena's] an idol of mine, both of them. I looked up to them growing up," Joint said in her post-match interview . "Just to be able to play them twice is amazing."

Serena struggled early, rarely landing her first serve and operating a step behind the pace of competition. She was broken on both of her service games in the first set, giving the seeded pair the early advantage.

The match got more competitive in the second set, with the teams remaining on serve all the way to the tiebreak, when the Williams sisters finally found the momentum they needed.

The two teams traded breaks in a thrilling third set, all the way up to Joint and Chan's comeback in the tiebreak. Venus in particular looked like the best player at the court for the final two sets.

Venus and Serena reportedly declined to speak with reporters after the match.

With the loss, the Williams sisters are now a combined 4-24 in singles and doubles action in 2026, numbers that don't count the US Open mixed doubles event and its significantly different rules. Joint is responsible for two of those losses, having beat Serena in the lone singles match of her much-talked about comeback.

The sisters lost their only other doubles match together, falling 2-6, 6-1, 10-8 to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns in the first round of Cincinnati last month.

Both sisters still playing is a testament to their love of tennis and competition, but the sport hasn't loved them back recently. Venus has lost 15 straight matches since opening her comeback last year with a win over Stearns, while Serena's return has been a start-and-stop affair due to a knee issue sustained in her singles match against Joint. Both are dependent on receiving wild-cards from tournaments looking for a draw, which isn't going to change anytime soon based on the reception they're still getting.

It remains to be seen where either player goes from here, with neither having anything to prove after their legendary careers. Serena has at least said she intends to play singles again, with the tournament TBD.

Even in a loss, however, they showed they can still produce the kind of moments their fans are looking for.

images.caption: Even in a loss, it's fun to see the Williams sisters play again. (Garrett Ellwood via Getty Images)

articles.title: Serena and Venus Williams lose in a match tiebreaker in their return to the US Open
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams are out of the US Open women’s doubles after losing in a match tiebreaker.
articles.body: Serena and Venus Williams were once again the main attraction at the US Open. Carlos Alcaraz sure wasn’t going to miss it. “I think there is no better plan (than) to watch the doubles, the Williamses once again, while getting a treatment,” the defending men’s champion said after winning his match. “I’m going to be ready for that.” The match was a thriller, with the sisters battling back to force a 10-point match tiebreaker, but then blowing a 5-0 lead and losing 6-3, 6-7 (6), 7-6 (10-7) on Friday night to Hao-Ching Chan and Maya Joint. It was the first U.S. Open match since 2022 at the Grand Slam tournament the sisters won twice. They battled back from 4-1 down in the third set to tie it, but then faltered late. Serena came back to tennis this year at 44. Venus has continued to play on tour at 46. Perhaps it was their ages, could have been Serena’s long layoff, or maybe it was nerves. But both double-faulted during the tiebreaker after they had played so brilliantly late in the third set and then in the first few points. The US Tennis Association said the sisters would not be available for comment. Serena ended up losing to Joint for the second time this summer. She fell to the Australian in three sets at Wimbledon in her return to singles play, and she and Venus then had to pull out of their doubles match after Serena hurt her knee. That delayed their return to the Grand Slam stage until New York, where they won in 1999 and 2009 and are now 27-8 in their 10 appearances. The match got a spot in the night session in Arthur Ashe Stadium — practically unheard of for first-round doubles. The sisters were once dominant in women’s doubles, teaming to win 14 Grand Slam titles along with Olympic gold medals in 2000, 2008 and 2012. They shared the No. 1 ranking in women’s doubles for eight weeks. It appeared a first-round loss in 2022 was their last time together, with Serena stepping away from tennis that year after winning 23 Grand Slam singles titles. She came back this summer and now has two heartbreaking defeats with her older sister. They also lost in a match tiebreaker at the Cincinnati Open. Venus Williams also lost in the first round of singles. Alcaraz won easily but two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka was finally challenged — by her opponent and by the smell of marijuana — in her victory. Sabalanka beat Kamilla Rakhimova 6-3, 6-4. The No. 1 seed was pushed in a second set that lasted 54 minutes — a minute longer than her entire previous match. Trying to become the first player to win three straight U.S. Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14, Sabalenka will face Taylor Townsend in the round of 16. Alcaraz returned to the round of 16 by beating Wu Yibing 6-3, 6-4, 6-1. Back for this tournament after missing four months because of a right wrist injury, the two-time champion will face No. 20 seed Tommy Paul, who edged No. 15 Alexander Bublik in five sets. “To be honest I’m better than I thought,” Alcaraz said.

images.caption: Serena and Venus Williams during their US Open first round women's double match up on Friday at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

articles.title: Serena & Venus Williams Top Stats, Highlights from Loss vs. Maya Joint, Hao-Ching Chan at US Open
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams weren't able defeat Maya Joint and Hao-Ching Chan despite a valiant effort at the 2026 US Open on Friday, suffering a 3-6, 7-6(6), 6-7(7) loss in their first-round women's doubles match.
articles.body:
Serena and Venus Williams weren't able defeat Maya Joint and Hao-Ching Chan despite a valiant effort at the 2026 US Open on Friday, suffering a 3-6, 7-6(6), 6-7(7) loss in their first-round women's doubles match.

It marked the first US Open doubles match for the Williams sisters since 2022.

Chan and Joint gained the upper hand early, winning three of the first four games in the opening set.

While Serena and Venus responded with a break and appeared to start getting more comfortable as the match continued, they still weren't able to take the first set.

The sisters fared much better in the second set, holding serve in the first game before gaining a 5-4 edge. They were still unable to convert break point opportunities against Chan and Joint, resulting in a tiebreaker.

While Serena and Venus won the first two points and later held a 6-4 advantage in the tiebreaker, a long forehand from Venus and a double fault from Serena resulted in a 6-6 score.

Still, the sisters were able to force a pair of mistakes by Joint in order to stay alive and secure a third set.

Chan and Joint took control of the third set early, gaining a 4-1 lead that was highlighted by a long backhand from Serena on break point in the fourth game.

The Williams sisters quickly got back on track, winning three straight games and bringing the score to 4-4.

Both duos held serve over the next four games, setting up a 10-point tiebreaker for the match.

Serena and Venus jumped out to a 5-0 lead in the tiebreaker, although Chan and Joint won eight of the next nine points to move back in front.

A long forehand from Serena set up match point before Chan hit a winner at the net to seal the final result.

The Williams sisters struggled with self-inflicted issues during the match, as they finished with 26 unforced errors compared to 15 for Chan and Joint.

Still, it was an admirable performance from the 46-year-old Venus and the 44-year-old Serena.

The sisters have already established themselves as a legendary duo, winning 14 Grand Slam women's doubles titles together and boasting a perfect 14-0 record in Grand Slam doubles finals.

articles.title: Venus and Serena Williams' highly anticipated US Open return ends in heartbreaking loss
articles.summary: Venus and Serena Williams returned to Arthur Ashe Stadium for a thrilling three-set US Open doubles match that kept fans on the edge of their seats.
articles.body: For the first time in four years, Venus and Serena Williams returned to the US Open court together Friday night in Queens. The legendary sisters were set to reunite earlier this summer at Wimbledon; however, Serena — who, at 44, is in the midst of a comeback after several years away from the sport — was forced to withdraw due to injury. Friday night, the two walked onto the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium to a massive ovation from the crowd. GROUP OF INFLUENCERS FORCES PAUSE DURING US OPEN MATCH WITH CRINGEWORTHY PHOTOSHOOT IN SUITE Serena's jacket listed her US Open titles, including the pair of doubles titles that she and Venus won in 1999 and 2009. Their opponents were Taiwan’s Chan Hao-ching and Australian Maya Joint, who, at 20 years old, was just a toddler when the Williams sisters won the 2009 US Open. The first set was fairly back and forth to start, but Chan and Joint pulled ahead to win it 6-3. The Williams sisters responded and started the second set strong, but it went the distance, needing a seven-point tie-breaker to decide the winner. In the tie-breaker, Venus and Serena had multiple opportunities to put Chan and Joint away, but they fought back. Finally, after the scare, the Williamses clinched the set to keep the match going. While they were respectful throughout the match, there was no question that the overwhelming majority of the crowd was behind the sisters, erupting after every point. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The tennis greats battled back against an impressive pairing that is only in their fourth event together to force a decisive tie-breaker in the final set. The Williamses took the first five points in a row to jump out to an early lead; however, Joint and Chan took the next three. Joint and Chan battled back to take the lead, and in the end, they walked away with the win in the match that was just a shade over three hours. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In the end, it was a fantastic three-set thriller, 6–3, 6–7(6), 7–6(10), that showed the Williams sisters — already all-time greats of the sport — are still a force to be reckoned with.

articles.title: US Open: Serena and Venus Williams suffer agonising defeat to Maya Joint and Chan Hao-Ching in a women's doubles first-round epic
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams suffer agonising defeat to Maya Joint and Chan Hao-Ching in a 10-point match tie-breaker at Flushing Meadows; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
In a fight to the finish, the Williams sisters rallied to force a third set tie-breaker in which they blew a 5-0 lead before falling to Joint and Chan 6-3 6-7 (8-6) 7-6 (10-7) in three hours and two minutes.

The legendary sister act were playing their first Grand Slam together since the 2022 US Open, and 27 years after they first won the title.

The comeback, which Serena said was at the suggestion ​of her daughter, carried the weight of more than two decades: 14 Grand Slam doubles titles together, two US Open crowns, three Olympic gold medals, and another 30 Grand Slam singles titles between ​them.

But it ended up being quite the summer for Joint, the 20-year-old Australian, who defeated Serena on Centre Court at Wimbledon in the women's singles before facing her in front of 23,000 adoring fans at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Friday night.

"Being able to play against such legends of the game is super special," said Joint on court.

"I'm lost for words to think of it," Joint continued. "She's my ​idol, both of them. I grew up in Michigan so I always looked up to ⁠them. Being able to play them twice is amazing."

It was certainly an occasion worthy of wild cards Serena, 44, and 46-year-old Venus were given as their every winner was cheered to the rafters of a packed stadium.

And there could be more to come from the 23-time Grand Slam champion after ESPN commentator Caroline Wozniacki revealed she believes Serena wants to return to singles next year.

They might have a combined age of 90 but the Williams' rolled back the years at times, and all of Ashe was on its feet when a penetrating Venus volley was put away by Serena's swinging winner.

But two breaks of Serena's serve - which had looked in good shape at Wimbledon and in her mixed doubles run-out with Carlos Alcaraz last week - cost them the first set.

They hit back in the second set tie-break, finally converting a fifth set point when a Joint overhead floated long.

The decider also rumbled into a tie-break, the the first time the duo had been past 5-5 in a third set since 2001.

But they stumbled badly in sight of the finishing line and a Chan volley ended the much-anticipated comeback.

The US Tennis Association said the sisters would not be available for comment following their defeat.

Greek star seals a career-first trip to the fourth round

Revitalised Stefanos Tsitsipas bounced back from a first-set loss to prevail over Czech 18th seed, Jiri Lehecka, with a 2-6 6-1 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 victory.

The Greek moved into the fourth round for ‌the first time in his career.

American 11th seed Frances Tiafoe eased past Valentin Vacherot from Monaco 6-4 6-2 6-4.

articles.title: US Open players can still be fined $50,000 for failing to fulfil little-known obligation even after defeat
articles.summary: Tennis News: Players at the US Open can incur a hefty $50,000 fine for not meeting post-match media requirements, even after their tournament run ends. Explore the obligations players must fulfill and the consequences of non-compliance.
articles.body: US Open players could be hit with a $50,000 fine if they fail to fulfil one of the tournament's lesser-known requirements, and the obligation can continue even after their hopes of winning the title are over.While the focus at Flushing Meadows is naturally on the matches and the record-breaking prize money on offer, players also have contractual responsibilities away from the court. One of those is attending the required media opportunities after each match.That means losing a match does not necessarily mean a player can simply pack their bags and leave.What happens if a US Open player refuses to speak to the media?According to page 49 of the Official Grand Slam Rulebook, players are required to attend post-match media opportunities at an appropriate and reasonable time following the conclusion of each match.Those obligations cover more than just the traditional press conference.The rule states that media opportunities include, but are not limited to, interviews with the host broadcaster and the player's national broadcaster. The singles champions also agree to participate in appropriate media activity when requested.A player who fails to comply can therefore face a $50,000 fine, unless they are unable to fulfil the obligation because of circumstances such as illness or injury.So, in practical terms, a player cannot simply lose a match and decide they would rather skip the questions before heading home. The media commitments remain part of their responsibilities throughout the tournament, including after elimination.There is already a recent example of how close a Grand Slam player can come to facing that punishment.At Wimbledon in July, Serena Williams chose not to attend her mandatory post-match press conference following her first-round defeat to Maya Short.Williams avoided a fine, however, after a quote attributed to her was released following the match. The All England Club determined that her decision not to attend was reasonable and that she had satisfied some of her media obligations by providing a response.At this year's US Open, no player had been fined for breaking the rule at the time of writing. But the potential punishment remains clear: $50,000 for failing to fulfil the required media duties, unless an accepted reason such as illness or injury applies.And it is not simply a US Open quirk. The issue has previously become one of the biggest talking points in tennis when a player decided they would rather not speak to the media at all.Naomi Osaka showed how serious the issue can becomeThe most famous example came in 2021, when Naomi Osaka withdrew from the French Open after refusing to participate in media duties.Osaka, who was world No.2 at the time, had announced before the tournament that she would not attend press conferences, explaining that she had experienced bouts of depression and social anxiety when engaging with the media.Grand Slam organisers subsequently warned that continued refusal to fulfil her media obligations could eventually lead to her being expelled from the tournament.Osaka ultimately chose to withdraw herself.In a lengthy statement, she explained that she believed leaving the tournament was the best decision for herself, the other players and the event.“This isn't a situation I ever imagined or intended when I posted a few days ago,” Osaka said.“I think now the best thing for the tournament, the other players and my wellbeing is that I withdraw so that everyone can get back to focusing on the tennis going on in Paris.”She also apologised for becoming a distraction and said she had struggled with depression since the 2018 US Open.“The truth is I have suffered long bouts of depression since the US Open in 2018 and I have had a really hard time coping with that,” she said.Osaka added that she was naturally introverted and that wearing headphones at tournaments helped with her social anxiety.French Tennis Federation president Gilles Moretton described her withdrawal as “unfortunate”, while also wishing her well and stressing that the Grand Slams, WTA, ATP and ITF remained committed to player wellbeing.The Osaka situation was ultimately about far more than a fine, but it demonstrated just how seriously Grand Slam organisers can take media obligations.At the US Open, the immediate consequence for a player who simply fails to fulfil the requirement is much easier to understand: $50,000 could be taken out of their pocket.And with the tournament's biggest stars still chasing the title at Flushing Meadows, that is one post-match responsibility they will probably want to remember.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz Explains Why He'll Take More Breaks During Tennis Season After Wrist Injury
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz revealed that he plans to take more breaks in 2027 after dealing with a wrist injury during the 2026 tennis season.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz revealed that he plans to take more breaks in 2027 after dealing with a wrist injury during the 2026 tennis season.

"I'm kind of a guy that doesn't need to play a lot of tournaments," Alcaraz said Friday, per the Associated Press (h/t ESPN ).

"I just feel like you can have those moments of time to have a break, to prepare well for tournaments, to prepare well mentally," he added.

The 23-year-old wrapped up a 6-3, 6-4, 6-1 victory over Wu Yibing in the third round of the US Open on Friday.

Alcaraz was previously sidelined for over four months due to a right wrist injury that he suffered at the Barcelona Open, causing him to miss Roland-Garros and Wimbledon.

He confirmed that he hasn't experienced any setbacks in his recovery during his current US Open run, though.

"It feels like I've been competing the whole time. So I surprise myself the way that I'm feeling and the way that I'm recovering after every match," Alcaraz said, via ESPN. "So I'm just really happy about it that I'm able to perform at my best after every match."

While a lighter schedule seems to be on the horizon for Alcaraz, he'll look to defend his 2025 US Open title and capture his eighth career Grand Slam championship for now.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Serena and Venus Williams prove they can still compete in Grand Slam doubles - but what does the future hold?
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams may have lost in their US Open doubles return, but the veteran pair proved they can still compete on an entertaining night in New York.
articles.body:
Rarely has a women's doubles first-round match headlined the US Open night session - but the Williams sisters are like no other pairing.

Serena and Venus Williams might have a combined age of 90, but their star remains undimmed. Neither does their ability to compete at the highest level when they are in tandem.

Even though the superstar siblings - aged 44 and 46 - lost on their highly-anticipated Grand Slam return, their performance in a narrow defeat by 14th seeds Hao-Ching Chan and Maya Joint led to an entertaining night in New York.

A packed Arthur Ashe Stadium roared on the American icons as they looked on course for a memorable win - but ultimately fell short in a 6-3 6-7 (6-8) 7-6 (10-7) loss.

"It was unbelievable how competitive that was," said former American player-turned-commentator Chanda Rubin, who lost to the Williams sisters in the 1999 US Open doubles final.

"After the first set you wondered if Serena and Venus would be able to find their mojo - but, boy, they did."

Four years after they last appeared on Ashe, the Williams sisters were given a rapturous reception as they strode onto a court where they have won eight singles titles between them and two doubles titles together.

The decibel levels were rarely matched in an underwhelming first set for the home favourites, but the noise quickly returned when they rallied in the second set.

The atmosphere became muted as the decider seemed to run away from them at 4-1 down, before they showed indomitable spirit - a hallmark of their extraordinary careers - to take their opponents into a first-to-10 match tie-break.

Racing into a 5-0 lead put the Williams sisters firmly on course to reach the second round, only for Chan and Joint to fight back - with the help of a double fault from each opponent.

Despite the initial despondency of the home fans, the volume was turned back up when the American pair were given a fond farewell - with everyone left wondering what the future holds for them both.

Serena hinted she wanted to play singles again in an interview with Good Morning America , external earlier this week, while Venus said after her singles exit on Monday that she should not "have to" think about her future beyond the doubles.

The questions about what happens next were not addressed by the pair following Friday's match. The sisters decided they were "not available" to speak to the media, US Open organisers said.

For once, the 20,000-odd fans on a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium sat quietly engrossed during points.

The sight of the Williams sisters back on court together at the US Open - possibly for the final time - commanded ultimate respect from a chatty crowd known to let their attention wander.

The siblings changed the face of the sport when they emerged as precocious teenagers in the 1990s, going on to dominate the sport with a combined 30 Grand Slam singles titles and 14 doubles victories as a pair.

Three decades later, the sport remains captivated by them.

Serena, a 23-time Grand Slam women's singles champion, coming out of retirement this summer sparked excitement among those who saw her in their prime and those too young to have witnessed it.

Seven-time major winner Venus has never "evolved away" from the sport - the words chosen by her younger sister when she last played in 2022 - but instead continued her career with the help of sporadic wildcards.

While that has proved controversial in some quarters, there were few objections about the sisters being invited to play once again at Flushing Meadows.

Their planned return at Wimbledon was scuppered by the knee injury which Serena suffered in her singles match there - ironically a defeat by 20-year-old Joint - before they finally reunited at the WTA event in Cincinnati.

The comeback ended in a match tie-break defeat by Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk and her American partner Peyton Stearns, with the same fate befalling them in New York.

When the Williams sisters last played on Ashe four years ago, they suffered a straight-set defeat by Czech pair Lucie Hradecka and Linda Noskova in the first round.

It looked like being a similar fate as they meekly surrendered the first set against Chan and Joint, then batted off four break points in the fifth and seventh games of the second set.

But once Serena upped her level to match her impressive sister, they managed to switch the momentum back in their favour and level the match.

An absorbing contest featuring some sensational points saw the Americans fight back again in the decider, only to falter from a commanding lead in the tie-break.

Overall it was a more than credible performance from the veteran pair. Their solid groundstrokes, sharp movement and never-say-die attitude caused problems for their opponents, who deserve huge credit for staying focused in a partisan environment.

"The atmosphere was surreal," said Joint.

"It was something we've never experienced before, and to play against such legends of the game was super special."
